id: title:eli-r-ph:faster burst detection for the global rate limiter

review.posthog_relevance: Changes the shared Redis-backed rate limiting and fleet-count accounting for PostHog's AI and token-distinct-id ingestion paths, unifying the time window and epoch to prevent shared counter splitting and under-counting, while adding an SRE-visible gauge and distinguishing never-synced cache entries.
review.reason: The observed changes implement a substantive, bounded improvement to the shared Redis rate limiting and fleet-count accounting. P1.F4 and P1.F6 unify the time window and epoch for shared counters, preventing silent counter splitting and under-counting across deployments. P1.F3 and P1.F6 ensure every event reaching the limiter is accounted for, preserving fleet-count parity. P1.F11.
review.uncertainty: The tier relies on the assumption that these shared Redis-backed paths are currently used or will be used in PostHog production; the provided observations do not independently verify active adoption or a specific incident avoided, only the implementation and its relevance to the shared dependency. No tier assignment is possible.

observations.behavior: Adds a new configuration option and shared-window enforcement for the AI byte budget, while removing a separate 'warned' counter and unifying the shared-rate-limit accounting.
observations.posthog_connection: This function unifies the window used for the shared Redis counter. It prefers the AI-specific window if set, otherwise falls back to the shared global rate limit window. This prevents the shared budget from splitting across deployments with different windows.

observations.behavior: Adds a window and its source env var to the LimiterSpec, and uses that window to compute the AI byte budget and the Redis epoch.
observations.posthog_connection: The AI byte budget is computed as the per-second limit multiplied by this window. The window also sets the Redis epoch, so all deployments sharing the same Redis key prefix must use the same window. This preserves the shared counter's correctness.

observations.behavior: Changes the shared-rate-limit accounting to charge every non-dropped event, including those already disabled, and removes the separate 'warned' counter.
observations.code_quote: // Charge every event, even one an event restriction already
observations.posthog_connection: This unifies the accounting: the shared Redis counter now counts all events that reach the limiter, regardless of whether person processing was already disabled. This prevents the shared budget from being undercounted and avoids discrepancies between the shared counter and the customer-facing warning.

observations.behavior: The shared token-distinct-id rate limiter is now charged for every event reaching this stage, including those whose person processing is already disabled, rather than skipping the limiter entirely. This preserves fleet-count parity with the v0 path.

observations.behavior: Adds a new gauge metric for the configured window interval, shared across deployments.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows PostHog SREs to compare the configured window interval across shared Redis deployments; mismatched values could cause epoch key divergence and silent counter splitting.

observations.behavior: Changes the CacheEntry.synced_at field from Instant to Option<Instant> to support never-synced entries.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the rate limiter to distinguish between entries that have never received a Redis sync and those that have, preventing premature decay of the fleet estimate.

observations.behavior: Adds a check for never-synced entries when deciding whether to queue a sync.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the rate limiter to immediately queue a sync for never-synced entries rather than waiting for a tier interval, reducing latency for newly discovered keys.
